description: The Tromsø Geophysical Observatory at UiT The Arctic University of Norway publishes geomagnetic data, ionosonde data, real-time and archive riometer data, all-sky camera images, geophysical reports and digitised records from 1843 onward for Tromsø, Dombås and Oslo, and hosts the Norwegian Center for Space Weather. Its geomagnetic data page offers archive and real-time magnetograms per station, stack plots, ASCII data to download or view (a password may be needed), real-time K-indices for the latest week, a Tromsø activity index since 1987 and a historical index for seven sites, daily and weekly mean values, and a real-time electrojet tracker, with links to partner networks such as DTU Space and the Finnish Meteorological Institute and advice for new users. Plots are open to view free of charge; no licence is stated on the pages read. Caveats: some ASCII data needs a password, and users are asked to read the note for new users before using the data. Coverage is Norway and the Arctic, with links to partner stations elsewhere. It supports hazard exposure analysis of geomagnetic storms for power grids, pipelines and GNSS at high latitudes; related records are Space Weather Canada and the INGV eSWua service.
